div.head: ECf 32 E 6
div.ab: Ita demum constituit et eis concessit bonus rex Edwardus, propinquus uester, — qui fuit optimus filius pacis — per commune consilium tocius regni. Qua de causa possunt et debent predicti de cetero nobiscum cohabitare et remanere in regno sicut coniurati fratres nostri et sicut proprii ciues regni.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 660 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 E …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

div.ab: So at last the good King Edward, your kinsman — who was the most excellent son of peace — decreed and granted to them, by the common counsel of the whole kingdom. For which reason the aforesaid can and ought henceforth to live together with us and remain in the kingdom as our sworn brothers and as own citizens of the kingdom.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Eadward III 4 (Verf. erinnert sich wieder der Maske des ECf-Buches, einer Agsächs. Jury, die Wilhelm den I. anredet; s. o. 32 A 8q; u. 35,1 A 1f); Eidbrüder 6; Reichsrat 6e. — Eadw.k Rs
Cf. Gl Eadward III 4 (the author again remembers the mask of the ECf book, an Anglo-Saxon jury addressing William I; see above, 32 A 8q; below, 35,1 A 1f); Eidbrüder 6; Reichsrat 6e. — Eadw.k Rs
